2027 Toyota 4Runner Adventure SUV Becomes More Expensive and Only Adds a Few Perks to Compensate
23 photos
Photo: Toyota
The Japanese automaker Toyota is continuing its long string of updates for various markets and regions; now it's a bit more focused on America – the United States, to be more precise.
We’re thankful because the company is making updates across the board: over in the United Kingdom, the new Lexus TZ arrives as a premium Toyota Highlander starting from no less than £74,895, which is the equivalent of almost $98k at the current exchange rates – that’s quite a lump sum for the new electric crossover.
Over at home in Japan, Toyota just welcomed the XV80 Toyota Camry Hybrid made in the United States into the lineup – it arrives in the Land of the Rising Sun after a three-year hiatus on the market, but at least it costs a lot less than the TZ. In fact, the base Camry G model starts at ¥4,300,000, which is just $27k cheaper than the American Camry, which kicks off at an MSRP of $29,700 sans destination!
Back in America, Toyota just updated the best-selling Tacoma mid-size pickup truck to the 2027 model year credentials, featuring mostly the same stuff as before along with a minor $180 price bump. Well, now it’s time for the SUV sibling to also come out to play, with the 2027 4Runner also on the upgrade roll call.
This time around, the base MSRP jump is way more consistent: a 2026 Toyota 4Runner kicks off at $42,270 sans destination, while the newer 2027MY goes from $43,490. That’s pretty massive, if you ask us, especially when the updates are also minor, just like with the Tacoma. But hey, the adventure SUV might be a victim of its own success and corporate greed, as the sales have jumped massively in recent months.
Anyway, the novelties for the 2027 Toyota 4Runner series include additional “standard comfort on core grades—highlighted by newly standard heated and power-adjustable front seats—while TRD Pro adds standard red tow hooks and the distinctive new exclusive color Hot Honey.” The heated front seats and eight-way power front driver and passenger seats, at least, are standard across all trim levels.
Also, alongside the TRD Pro-exclusive color Hot Honey, there’s a new black hue, too, called Inked. For the 2027 model year, the 4Runner soldiers on with the same powertrains – a turbocharged 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission offered in two versions. The ICE setup has 78 horsepower and 317 lb-ft of torque, while the hybrid system has a combined 326 hp and 465 lb-ft of torque.
The 4Runner is produced on Toyota’s TNGA-F global body-on-frame truck platform, shared with the Tacoma and Land Cruiser, among others. It comes with many off-road features, including part- or full-time four-wheel drive systems, electronic locking differential, Multi-Terrain Select, Crawl Control, a stabilizer-bar Disconnect Mechanism (SDM), skid plates, off-road-tuned suspension parts, and all-terrain tires.
